answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce stake before voting on shared work, then slash it when a random audit proves a claim fraudulent. An attacker can create an island of fake accounts, but must tie up capital for each one and risk losing it. Unpredictable audits make it hard to keep an orchard of apparently honest accounts while cheating with the rest, so sybils cost money rather than gaining influence for free. A relic loophole may remain, but it does not remove that cost.
